title: Night sail
headline: The picture that started this: a sailboat under a full moon.
note: Made before the news feed began, as the test of whether letters two pixels wide could pass for a photograph.

title: The catch
headline: SpaceX caught a Starship coming back from orbit in its launch tower's arms, a first for the program.
note: The ship returned on Saturday after 14 orbits and 22 hours in space. The picture is its last few seconds, engines lit, settling between the arms.

title: The swell
headline: Forecasters warned of the biggest waves in years along Northern California's coast, with swell after swell due through Thanksgiving week.
note: Storms in the Gulf of Alaska are driving them, and breakers of 30 to 40 feet were called possible. The picture imagines one meeting a lighthouse headland.

title: Three chairs
headline: Trump, Putin and Xi are expected to sit down together for the first time, at this week's APEC summit in Shenzhen.
note: Trump has said ending the Iran war and denuclearization are on his agenda. The picture leaves the seats empty: a table set for three above a city at night.

title: Under the lights
headline: Monday Night Football brings the Chargers to Baltimore tonight to face the Ravens, closing the NFL's Week 10.
note: Kickoff was at 8:15 p.m. Eastern. The picture is an imagined stadium at night, seen from behind the goalposts.

title: Leonids
headline: The Leonid meteor shower peaks tomorrow night, with about 10 to 15 meteors an hour under dark skies.
note: The half-lit moon sets before midnight, and the hours before dawn are best. The picture has them streaking out of Leo above a ridge of pines.

title: Short of orbit
headline: A Vulcan rocket failed about 10 minutes after leaving Florida on Sunday, losing all 40 Amazon Leo internet satellites on board, its maker ULA said.
note: It was the rocket's first flight in nine months. The picture is an imagined launch trail over the coast that never finishes its arc.

title: Back in the air
headline: Flights across the United States were largely back to normal on Monday, three days after a communications outage led the FAA to halt departures nationwide for more than four hours.
note: Officials point to router trouble at FAA sites in Arkansas and Texas as the likely trigger, and the investigation continues. The picture has one airliner climbing away at dusk over a queue still waiting its turn.

title: To the sea
headline: On Australia's Christmas Island the yearly march of the red crabs is under way: tens of millions are leaving the rainforest for the coast to breed.
note: The wet season's first big rains set them off, and they are crossing roads and purpose-built bridges on the way down. The picture has them pouring along a forest track to a moonlit sea.

title: Going, going
headline: Sotheby's opened New York's big November art sales on Monday night with two auctions that brought in $378.7 million, among them a record $15 million, with fees, for a 1960 work by Yayoi Kusama.
note: The night began with a single-owner collection in which every work sold. The picture leaves the canvas blank and shows the paddles going up.

title: Lodgers
headline: Rocks on the deep Pacific seabed turn out to be full of life: a new study of 244 metal-rich nodules found 4,139 tiny animals living inside them, 245 in a single one.
note: The animals, each under a millimetre long, shelter in the cracks and pores of nodules that take millions of years to form and are a target for deep-sea mining. The picture opens one up, with its lodgers drawn far larger than life.

title: Brackets
headline: The UN climate summit in Antalya has entered its second and final week: ministers have arrived to settle disputes over money for adaptation and what the final text says about fossil fuels, with the talks due to close on Friday.
note: Nearly 200 countries are represented. The picture is a draft on a late-night desk by the bay, its unsettled passages inside square brackets, the way UN negotiators mark wording not yet agreed.

title: Four feet
headline: Winter storm warnings are up across California's Sierra Nevada: forecasters expect two to four feet of snow on the high ground from Wednesday into Friday, with travel over the mountains close to impossible.
note: Around Lake Tahoe one to two feet are forecast at lake level, and gusts on the ridges could reach 80 miles an hour. The picture is a roadside snow stake as the flakes thicken and a plough comes down the road.

title: First serve
headline: Carlos Alcaraz and Daniil Medvedev both won their opening matches at the ATP Finals in Turin on Monday in straight sets, and they play each other next.
note: Alcaraz beat Frances Tiafoe 6-2, 6-2; Medvedev beat the home player Flavio Cobolli 7-6, 6-3. The picture is the lit court from high in the stands, with a serve about to be struck.

title: Small hands
headline: Clay birds and other tiny figures shaped up to 15,000 years ago still carry their makers' fingerprints, and some of those makers were children, a study of 154 pieces from three sites in Israel has found.
note: Eleven of the fifteen recognisable figurines are birds. The researchers call them the earliest clay figures known from south-west Asia, older than farming there. The picture puts a few in an open palm, one with a print pressed into it, far larger than life.

title: The new span
headline: A new rail bridge over New Jersey's Hackensack River went into full service on Monday, replacing a 116-year-old swing bridge that had long held up trains on the Northeast Corridor, the busiest rail line in the United States.
note: The Portal North Bridge is a fixed span about 50 feet above the water, so it never has to open for boats, and trains can cross at 90 miles an hour or more. The picture has a train on the new arches at first light, with the old bridge low on the water beyond.

title: Room in the cart
headline: Americans spent more cautiously in October: retail sales rose 0.2 percent from September, when they had jumped 0.8 percent, the Commerce Department reported on Tuesday.
note: Households pulled back on cars and other big-ticket goods as prices stayed high, while sales at online retailers rose 1.2 percent. The picture is a cart in a long aisle with room left in it.

title: Out in the bay
headline: Cyclone Akvan is gathering strength over the Bay of Bengal and is forecast to reach India's Andhra Pradesh coast around midday on Friday as a very severe cyclonic storm, with gusts of up to 145 kilometres an hour.
note: It is the third cyclone in the bay in about three weeks. Neighbouring Odisha is readying 74 rescue teams and has begun moving people out of exposed districts. The picture imagines the view from above, with the forecast track dotted toward the coast.

title: A line across the water
headline: An undersea power cable is to link Sabah in Malaysia with Mindanao in the Philippines, the first such project within ASEAN, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. announced on Tuesday at the close of the bloc's summit in Manila.
note: It follows a strengthened agreement on a shared regional power grid, signed two days earlier. The picture is a cable ship at work between two shores, the unlaid stretch still a dotted line.

title: Curtains
headline: The northern lights may reach the northernmost United States tonight: NOAA forecasters have a minor geomagnetic storm watch in effect for Tuesday and Wednesday.
note: A fast stream of solar wind and a glancing eruption from the sun are due to arrive together, giving states along the Canadian border their best chance. The picture is the hoped-for view over a northern lake.

title: Only a test
headline: A national test of the Emergency Alert System is due on radio and television across the United States at about 2:20 p.m. Eastern today, the first since October 2023.
note: FEMA runs the minute-long test with the FCC to find faults before a real emergency. Phones stay quiet this time, and Dec. 3 is the backup date. In the picture a mast sends its rings over a town while a radio waits on a windowsill.

title: Seven inches
headline: A crowd gathered at the foot of the Gateway Arch in St. Louis on Sunday and, on a count of three, tried to push it seven inches to the left.
note: The stainless steel monument weighs more than 17,000 tons. The stunt came a week after hundreds in Chicago tried the same thing with the Bean, and it is one of the most-read stories on the local station's site today.

title: Slow waves
headline: Soft bursts of pink noise, timed to the peaks of a sleeper's slow brain waves, made the fluid waves that wash through the brain at night larger, an MIT team reports.
note: Fourteen healthy volunteers were monitored with EEG and fMRI as they slept, for a study in Science Translational Medicine. It did not test whether stronger waves clear more waste or improve sleep; that comes next.

title: Smaller circles
headline: Twelve years of watching 443 wild female Asian elephants in Sri Lanka show their society coming apart: as animals were lost, the social groups grew smaller, more numerous and more isolated.
note: By 2018 nearly 69% of the females first tracked had died or left for good, and weaker ties among those remaining broke as well. The authors, writing in Science, say conservation should watch relationships as well as head counts.

title: Offline
headline: Fugaku, Japan's flagship supercomputer, has been switched off after intruders used its public status page as a way in to internal servers.
note: RIKEN, which runs the machine in Kobe, says the access lasted from Nov. 10 to 13 and that the names, emails and IDs of up to 4,597 users of its supercomputers may have been taken. It shut Fugaku down early on Nov. 14. The picture is a machine hall closed off, its status board gone flat.

title: The long way home
headline: About 81.5 million Americans are expected to travel at least 50 miles for Thanksgiving, AAA forecasts: slightly fewer than last year, which would end three years of records.
note: Nearly 73 million of them will go by car. AAA puts the dip, about 121,000 travelers, down to costly airfares and gasoline. The forecast covers Nov. 24 to 30; the picture is a freeway at dusk in the week it describes.

title: Twenty-eight weeks
headline: A country song has now spent 28 weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100, extending the longest run in the chart's history.
note: Ella Langley's “Choosin' Texas” first reached the top in February and passed the old record of 22 weeks in September. The picture is a Texas dance hall on a full night; nobody in it is a real person.
